contracts.description: HTTP surface exposed by the Calling service: health, the call API (list, get, available actions), application call creation and control (accept, decline, cancel, end, hold, resume, transfer, session removal, media credentials), the endpoint registry, signaling-credential minting, the endpoint's signaling operations (WebSocket channel, offer recovery, accept / decline, media credentials) and the media provider callback; the platform credential, signaling credential and provider signature schemes; the error envelope. No generic state mutation.

Canonical call-domain vocabulary (Part C sections 15-25): the 17 call states, call kind, normalized failure categories, terminal reasons, participant roles, session states, endpoint categories, call event types, the call representation (CallCore / CallSummary), ring-offer, media-access, transfer and endpoint vocabularies, server-authorized media capabilities and the bounded safe event data object.

Payload of every call event published through Calling's transactional outbox inside the cfmeet.platform.event-envelope: ids, scope, gap-free sequence, call version, states, time, correlation id and safe data. Provider-independent; no telephone numbers, provider ids, credentials or tokens.

Request and response bodies of the application-calling API (Part C sections 20-25): call creation, ring-offer answers, cancel / end / hold / resume / transfer and their results, session removal, available actions, the ring-offer and transfer representations, media credentials, endpoints, signaling credentials and offer recovery. No client-chosen scope, state, permission or provider data; no provider identifiers or administrative capabilities in responses.

Frames of an endpoint's realtime signaling channel: call signals (call.incoming ... call.invitation_expired) derived from committed state and sent after commit, with event id, call id, version / sequence, target endpoint and principal, safe state, issue time, offer expiry, correlation id and a bounded payload; and the channel control frames. No telephone numbers, provider ids, credentials or tokens.

Transport-neutral push-ready payload of a ring offer (call id, offer id, call kind, optional caller display name, issue and expiry times) for a future push service. No media credential, provider token, API credential or telephone number.
Shared definitions: service identity, runtime environment, request/correlation ids, UUIDs, application environment kind, principal kind, key ids, internal permissions.
JOSE header of internal service tokens (EdDSA pinned).
Claims of internal service tokens: issuer, exact audience, runtime environment, short lifetime, token id, signed request and correlation ids, optional delegated context.
Safe customer/application/actor identifiers carried inside a signed service token.
Receiver-controlled trust policy: trusted issuers, Ed25519 public keys and locally granted internal permissions.
Internal service-to-service HTTP conventions: service auth security scheme, request/correlation headers, normalized internal auth errors.
Envelope for durable cross-service events. Payload contracts are registered separately by the producing service (Calling: cfmeet.calling.call-lifecycle-event).
